children.title: VLCC
children.summary: No material change in the VLCC market, still strong by any measure. However, there are signs which could suggest it's levelling out, which would not be too surprising.

children.title: Suezmax
children.summary: There has been reasonable activity to start the week. However, the market remains very much oversupplied, with 17 FOC and 7 ETS 5 day window ETA West Africa by 10 September.

children.title: Aframax
children.summary: North Sea After the large number of vessels we have seen ballast towards the US the North Sea list has been left with a reduced number of natural candidates for North Sea business. Dates have pushed into early September with rates picking.

children.title: Capesize
children.summary: This week on Capesize we saw strong demand from Pacific C5 as three majors were seen in the market alongside a healthy showing of supportive operators. Recent bids seen at mid to high USD 15 levels and today a Newcastlemax fixed at low USD 15 C5 equivalent.

children.title: Panamax
children.summary: The Panamax market has firmed steadily through the week, with the index posting consecutive gains and sentiment improving across both basins. The Pacific has been the clearer engine: NoPac and Australian grain and coal demand has absorbed the prompt tonnage that had been weighing on the market, and owners are now comfortable holding their levels while charterers chase.

children.title: Supramax
children.summary: The Supramax market remained largely subdued and stable. The Atlantic was mixed, with the Mediterranean gradually softening while the Continent saw some fresh enquiry and the US Gulf and South Atlantic remained broadly balanced.
